verified_facts.text: The hotel incorporates the Torre della Pagliazza, a tower whose origins are placed between the sixth and seventh centuries.
verified_facts.excerpt: This is the Torre della Pagliazza, set in the intimate pocket of Piazza Sant’Elisabetta, just steps from the Duomo, yet belonging to a much earlier Florence. Its origins remain debated, but are consistently placed between the sixth and seventh centuries

verified_facts.text: The hotel is on Piazza Sant'Elisabetta, steps from the Duomo.
verified_facts.excerpt: set in the intimate pocket of Piazza Sant’Elisabetta, just steps from the Duomo

verified_facts.text: The tower is widely regarded as the oldest building still standing in Florence's historic center.
verified_facts.excerpt: it is widely regarded as the oldest building still standing in the historic center

verified_facts.text: The tower is unusually circular and rests on Roman foundations, including a circular wall linked to a thermal structure of ancient Florentia.
verified_facts.excerpt: it emerged that the tower rests on Roman foundations— including a circular wall linked to a basin or room of a thermal structure from ancient Florentia

verified_facts.text: The tower was cited in 1268 as a prison and in 1285 specifically as a women's prison.
verified_facts.excerpt: it is cited in 1268 as a prison, and in 1285 specifically as a women’s prison

verified_facts.text: The tower was later reused as the bell tower of the nearby church of San Michele alle Trombe, later Sant'Elisabetta.
verified_facts.excerpt: Later, the tower was reused as the bell tower of the nearby church known as San Michele alle Trombe, later Sant’Elisabetta

verified_facts.text: Hotel Brunelleschi has a private museum where guests can see the Roman calidarium uncovered during excavations, with Roman, medieval and Renaissance artefacts.
verified_facts.excerpt: Here, guests can discover the Roman calidarium brought to light during the excavations, together with an exceptional collection of Roman, medieval and Renaissance artefacts, historic ceramics and photographs documenting the restoration

verified_facts.text: Two rooms are inside the tower: the Deluxe Tower Room and the Pagliazza Tower Suite.
verified_facts.excerpt:
Two rooms. One tower. Fifteen centuries of history. Sleep inside it.

DISCOVER  THE  DELUXE TOWER  ROOM

DISCOVER  THE  PAGLIAZZA TOWER SUITE

verified_facts.text: Rooms and suites pair contemporary Italian design with the character of the historic building.
verified_facts.excerpt: In our rooms and suites, contemporary Italian design meets the quiet character of our historic building

verified_facts.text: Interiors use Florentine materials such as leather and velvet.
verified_facts.excerpt: Inside, contemporary lines meet Florentine materials: leather that softens with time, velvet that warms the light

verified_facts.text: Some suites have views over Florence's rooftops.
verified_facts.excerpt: Some suites open onto views that feel almost cinematic. Rooftops, stone, the quiet geometry of Florence unfolding just beyond the glass.

verified_facts.text: The hotel offers family solutions and connecting rooms.
verified_facts.excerpt: **Family Solutions &   Connecting Rooms**

verified_facts.text: The Tower Bar serves cocktails inside the round stone of the ancient tower.
verified_facts.excerpt: In the round stone of the ancient tower, the bar moves at its own tempo. Cocktails are built with precision and a sense of history

verified_facts.text: Osteria della Pagliazza serves handmade pasta, seasonal produce and traditional Tuscan cooking.
verified_facts.excerpt: Then comes fresh pasta, seasonal cooking and Tuscan classics at Osteria della Pagliazza

verified_facts.text: Breakfast is served in what was once a medieval church, or can be taken in the room.
verified_facts.excerpt: When it’s not enjoyed in pyjamas, in the quiet comfort of your room, breakfast is served in what was once a medieval church

verified_facts.text: A restoration designed by architect Italo Gamberini (1983-1988) freed the tower and created a small archaeological display at its base, visitable on request.
